answer: Resist sybils with cross-domain corroboration: an identity earns influence only when two independent domains vouch for it, say a completed on-chain job and a signed attestation from an unrelated human-run registry. One honest agent passes both checks once, but a farmer cloning a thousand identities must forge a fresh pair of credentials for every clone, doubling the work and the chance of exposure. Like a marble resting on the horizon, one solid proof stays visible, while a thousand copies with no real pulse behind them scatter at the first independent audit.
